lines.en: I knock on Ami’s door.
I knock on Ami’s door.
: Coming!
Ami arrives at the large wooden rectangle currently preventing me from entering her room.
Most people would refer to this as a “door” but I personally think doors are useless when you could always tear through the wall and force your way into places.
Unless those walls are made of metal.
In those cases, rare as they may be, tearing through anything will not work.
You must find special tools and cut.
Or saw.
Thankfully, I don’t need to do anything like this tonight.
: Hi!
: Hey. Where are your pants?
: Who cares?
: Good point.
: I’m not interrupting any “alone time,” am I?
: It wouldn’t make much of a difference if you were.
: It's not like you haven't already caught me in the act before, right?
: True. But, to be fair, the door was locked. So it's not like that one time really counts or anything.
: Of course! Masturbating behind a locked door is basically the same thing as never masturbating at all!
: Uhh...sure. That makes sense.
: Besides...and this isn't me saying that any of that kind of stuff was gonna happen tonight...but I’m glad you showed up because that means we get to talk instead!
: I obviously can’t speak for you, but I personally gain a lot more pleasure from...well, pleasure than casual conversation.
: Who says it has to be casual? Maybe I want to talk about wires what you ate for lunch today or where we go when we die what you ate for lunch today?
: That’s a good idea. Let’s talk about what I ate for lunch today.
I decide to talk to Ami about what I ate for lunch today.
The conversation falls flat when I realize I can’t remember if I even ate anything at all.
And that would be no good. Ten out of ten doctors agree that if you don’t eat things, you will likely die.
I don’t want to die yet.
If I die, how will I get to eat lunch tomorrow?
: So, Sensei...I’ve been doing some thinking, and I think it would be good if we got a new house together.
: Oh, sure. Let me just buy a new house in the spur of the moment because you’ve been doing some thinking.
: Yay!
: Ami, we’re not buying a new house.
: AAAaaAAAHAhAHAHAHAAAA!@!!!!!!!!
Ami throws a temper tantrum as if she were a little girl.
The only thing is that I can’t personally confirm if it’s the same type of tantrum she’d throw when she was really little because her parents didn’t die until she was seven.
: Aren’t you going to ask the reason I wanted to buy a new house, Sensei?
: I wasn’t planning on it since it definitely isn’t going to happen, but sure.
: Because I love you!
: That is not a suitable reason for a purchase that large.
: But if we get a bigger house, there will be a larger number of square feet in which we can get our love all over each other.
: We haven’t even gotten our love all over our current house yet.
: Well then hurry up and pour it all over me, [amimaster].
: Fill buckets and buckets with your love juice and dump it right onto my adorable little head.
: We can even leave the front door open so if somebody shows up, they can catch us in the act and then probably cry because everyone thinks they love you for some reason.
: Wow. You’re even more possessive than normal today.
: Do you really not want a new house, though? Even though our current one is filled with sad memories?
: There are good memories too. I just can’t remember most of them yet.
: I guess. But doesn’t it get annoying having people just show up all the time when we want to be alone together?
: Ami, can you let me in? I forgot my key...
: See what I’m talking about? We’ve barely even gotten each other’s clothes off and Maya is already trying to come between us.
: Maya? I didn’t hear Maya.
: Are you asleep or something? What’s going on?
: Oh. I heard her that time.
: Hold on, Maya! I’ll be there in a second! Just have to put my underwear back on!
: Why would you say that? Now I’m either going to have to deal with her calling me disgusting again or hide under the bed until she leaves.
: Well that’s no good. Sometimes, Maya doesn’t leave the room for days. You could very well starve to death, [amimaster].
: And if you starve to death, how am I going to ride you cowgirl style anymore?
: Okay, seriously...open the door.
: Hold on one second, Sensei. I have to go do something really quick.
: 了解です。
Ami gets off the bed and I stare at her butt for a few seconds before she makes it to the door.
It’s a good butt. The kind that you want to grab and squeeze and then have her jump because you’re actually in a train and she’s never seen you before.
Lol.
: Who’s there?
: Are you kidding? It’s me. Open the door.
: Name and age, please.
: Maya Makinami, age- Wait, why am I identifying myself for you? Just let me in. I live here.
: Sorry, Maya. But I’m a little busy right now.
: Sensei and I haven’t gotten to be alone together as much as I want lately, and you’re kind of getting in the way with all of your knocking.
: Sensei is in there?
: Hey, Maya. What did you eat for lunch today?
: Don’t ask her that, Sensei. She obviously just ate a WATERMELON.
: Hahahahahahahahahahah!
: Hahahahahahahahahahah!
: Hahahahahahahahahahah!
: Hahahahahahahahahahah!
: Open the fucking door.
: Woah! No one’s ever going to marry you if you have that kind of attitude, Maya.
: Ami, I’m not kidding.
: I don’t know what’s going through your head right now but-
: Sensei, Maya doesn’t want us to be alone together...
: She thinks we’re up to something weird even though we’re related.
: I just want to sit on your lap like I’m a little girl again and talk about lunch, but she’s being meeeeaaaaaan~~~~~
: Maybe we should just let her-
: No.
: I don’t want to let her in.
: This is our time together.
: Maya, here’s an idea! How about you come back in half an hour or so? There’s something I need to talk to Sensei about.
: Why? What do you need to talk to him about?
: Why do you care? You hate Sensei.
: Right. He’s horrible. But what do you need to talk to him about?
: Why do you care?
: Because if it’s something involving me, I-
: Why would it be something involving you?
: You’re not secretly hiding some sort of relationship with my [uncle] from me, are you?
: No! I just-
: Can you just please open the door?...
: What do you think? Should we open it?
DON’T OPEN THE DOOR
: Of course not. We’re not done talking yet.
THE DOOR DOES NOT NEED TO BE OPENED
: We don’t have to open it. Not if you haven’t said everything you want to say yet.
ALL OF THE GOOD THINGS ARE HERE
: All of the good things are already in here. Opening the door would just let the bad things in.
STAY IN THE ROOM ALONE
: We should stay in here without Maya. I don’t feel like talking about the stars.
MAYA IS A FUCKING NERD
: Maya’s a fucking nerd. She can wait in the hall.
STAY WITH YOUR NIECE
: I would rather be with my [niece] alone. She’s the only one who understands me.
: Well, there you have it. Please come back later after Sensei and I are done loving each other.
: As [niece] and [uncle], of course. We’d neeeeeeeeeeeeeeever be anything more than that.
: I am a respectable man with morals and-
: OPEN THE FUCKING DOOR!
Ami and I slowly back away from the wooden rectangle and Maya, who doesn’t appear to know that you can just cut your way into rooms, ultimately retreats.
Either that or she goes silent and slopes downward in the hall to [masturbate] to the thought of an [incest]uous [uncle]/[niece] pairing.
The only thing is that there are other girls in the hallway today and, if any of them saw her touching herself out there, they’d probably say something.
Unless it’s Rin. If it’s Rin, she’ll probably offer to finger Maya herself.
And then she’ll probably convince herself she’s fallen in love with her too.
They’d make a cute couple.
Thankfully, there’s no one else in the hall right now (At least to my knowledge), so she’d be able to get away with it.
: So, now that we’ve gotten rid of Maya, there are a few more things I’d like to talk about.
: Are you in the right mindset yet, [amimaster]? Or do you need a little more time to regain your footing?
: Right mindset? What do you mean?
: I just got here, didn’t I?
: Right. You knocked on the door and immediately came to sit on my bed with me.
: Nothing happened in between those two things. And everything is completely okay now.
: You’re completely okay now. Ami’s got you.
: You’re being kind of weird.
Ami sits up on the bed, fixing her posture but spreading her legs apart more.
She smells faintly of shampoo so I imagine she just took a shower.
And, on another note, I feel strangely out of place right now.
Have you ever found yourself in a situation where you think you’re there, but you’re not really there?
Like you can comprehend the things hanging around you, but all of them are swaying so rapidly that you can’t find it in yourself to burn them into your mind.
To etch them into the gray walls of your cerebral cortex and really start to understand exactly what is happening and not just “what’s happening.”
This is one of those times.
So, I slap myself in the face and put myself back into serious mode, because I’m pretty sure Ami wants to have an actual conversation about something more than just relocating right now.
: We’re both being kind of weird.
: We do that sometimes.
: But we’ve seen and felt horrible things together, so we share a bond that not many other people do.
: It’s a bond that makes it okay for the two of us to “black out” at times.
: I think that’s how we used to describe it in the past, isn’t it?
: If you remember the past at all, that is.
: Your memory has never been that good, [amimaster].
: To be completely honest, I can’t even tell if it’s been getting better or worse lately.
: It’s like every time I start to remember something, there’s a brief flash and TV static.
: Like that.
: That’s completely normal. And it’s okay for you to feel that way.
: Because, even if you start doing weird stuff, it’s not like I’ll ever say no to anything.
: You could honestly pin me down and ravage me in the middle of[school] one day and I’d lay there and take it like the good girl I am.
: I don’t think that’s a thing that will be happening any time soon.
: Of course it won’t be happening any time soon. Or probably ever.
: There are too many people who would be hurt by it.
: You know, one of the many many many many many many many reasons I love you is because, even though you pretend not to, you really do care about everyone.
: You’ve always been that way. It’s the same reason you decided to take in an orphaned girl when she had nowhere else to go.
: Even when you were just as sad as her and had broken into a million pieces of your own.
: And so we did what we had to do and finished each other’s puzzles.
: You were what I needed you to be, and I was what you needed me to be.
: Everything else was just static.
: But once that static got louder...that’s when things started getting weird.
: I’m guessing that’s when you started realizing you were in love with me?
: That’s not what I’m talking about.
: I’m talking about when you started going back to normal.
: When you stopped being so sad all the time and started putting things back together without my help.
: It was nice seeing you learn to walk again, but I missed having to be the little girl who would hold you up with her big hugs and her infectious smile.
: I don’t want to say you were drifting away because we were still really close-
: But I could tell there was something else there. Something that was preventing us from being closer.
: You started coming home a little later some nights.
: And then even later than that some other nights.
: And it didn’t really occur to me until a couple years ago, but that wasn’t just because of tutoring, was it?
: I...honestly have no idea.
: How come you never really tutored anyone at our house, Sensei?
: I already told you. I have no idea.
: But if I had to take a guess, it’s because it would have been weird to invite girls of that age over to a middle-aged guy’s house without parental supervision.
: I can’t imagine any of those parents would be thrilled about that either.
: Are you sure you weren’t just trying to keep your “work” life and your personal life separate?
: Again, I don’t know.
: You don’t know?
: No. And why are you asking about this right now?
: What does what I did for work back then have to do with us?
: This is hardly normal [uncle]/[niece] bonding, Ami.
: I guess it is a little random to talk about it out of nowhere like this, but I’ve been thinking really hard about some stuff lately.
: I’m sure it’s not true, but I keep thinking that maybe something happened with you while I wasn’t around that hurt you really bad.
: Because, somewhere along the line, you gave up on tutoring. And I never really understood why.
: Probably because it didn’t pay well enough to support taking care of you.
: Would the answer really be that simple? Or would it be something a little more complicated?
: Complicated?
: Like Noriko, maybe?
: I mean. Noriko is definitely complicated, but I don’t think I’d ever quit tutoring because of her.
: Maybe Maya then?
: Maya is also complicated, but I don’t think I’d quit over tutoring her-
: But you never tutored Maya.
: Wait, what?
: You never tutored Maya, Sensei.
: She wasn't one of your students.
: You didn’t meet her until I started bringing her home in middle[school].
: Unless you were hiding her from me, that is.
: But why would you be hiding another girl my age from me when I could have become friends with them?
: You had no problems with Ayane when I started bringing her home.
: Have you actually known Maya this whole time?
: Have you just been pretending not to know her?
: And if so, why?
: I don’t understand.
Now that I think about it, every time I’ve tried talking to Ami about Maya’s past, she’s seemed almost completely oblivious.
Ayane, too.
Neither of them knew anything about her family. Just where she came from and when she showed up.
: You two don’t like each other. That much is very clear to me.
: So why, if you have known each other for that long, are you pretending not to?
: Do you think that maybe someone is just playing a trick on you, [amimaster]?
: Do you think that someone could be taking advantage of your bad memory to make you think things are real that aren’t actually real?
: Do you know what is real, though?
: The past you have with me.
: Not the past of girls that you’d see during designated hours five or six days a week.
: The past you have with the girl who would bleach the maggots out of your room for you or sponge bathe you when you couldn’t bring yourself to get out of bed.
: That past is real.
: Tell me you see me.
: Tell me you see me, not the fake memories of someone else who thinks they love you.
: When you love someone, you don’t have to hide it.
: So either everything is fake...or you’ve been hiding something very bad from me for a very long time...
: Or you’re just misremembering and talked about tutoring Maya on accident!
: In fact, since your memory is so bad, I’m sure that’s exactly what happened.
: So I won’t annoy you about it any more.
: At least not until something else slips out that makes me think, “Hmm...is my [uncle] less amazing than I thought he was?”
: Because right now, I still think you’re the most amazing, most handsome person in the entire world.
: With the biggest penis of all time.
: And I want to have cute [incest] babies with you and watch them live long, happy, healthy lives.
: Oh! Maya’s back!
: Oh. And you’re here, too.
: Would you mind explaining why I had to use my key to unlock your door when you’re clearly capable of opening it on your own?
: It’s fine to have fights with your roommates, but dragging me into them is just a waste of my time.
: What happened in here?
: I’m not sure.
: Well, whatever it was, please keep a tighter leash on your [niece].
: I would love that.
: Please.
: Ami...
: Yes, Maya?
: I already told you there’s nothing going on. You didn’t need to go this far to prove-
: Hm? Sensei and I just talked about lunch and stuff.
: I have no idea what you’re talking about.
: I think it’s probably best if we leave the two of them to resolve this on their own.
: You’re clearly involved in this somehow and-
: Sensei isn’t involved at all. He was just spending time with his favorite girl in the world.
: Makoto’s right, though. I definitely think I should start heading home for the night.
: I’m sad, but I understand.
: I’ll see you in the morning, though. I bought chocolate chips for pancakes, too, so expect a really big breakfast!
: That...
: That sounds great...
What exactly happened tonight?
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
